折.meaning: An <part>anchor</part> pins down a huge map that won't close. An <part>axe</part> waits beside it. One whack straight down the middle, a sharp crease, and the map will finally <kanji>fold</kanji>.
折.on: A setter dog grabs the folded map in its mouth and runs off with it. The first part of setter, 'set': <reading>せつ</reading>.
折.kun: You fold the paper again and again until it's a tiny paper crane: origami. Keep just the start, 'oh-ree': <reading>おり</reading>.

合.meaning: An <part>umbrella</part>-shaped lid drops onto a <part>one</part>-plank rim over a <part>mouth</part>-shaped box. Click! Lid and box were made for each other: a perfect <kanji>fit</kanji>.
合.on: A goat tries the lid on as a hat, and it fits the goat too. Goat without the t, a held 'goh': <reading>ごう</reading>.
合.kun: 'Ah! Ooh!' you say as the lid clicks into place. Ah-oo: <reading>あう</reading>. <ja>合う</ja> is to fit or suit.

羊.meaning: A <part>king</part> wakes up with curly <part>horns</part> poking out over his crown and wool sprouting down his back. His court tries very hard not to laugh. Overnight he has turned into a <kanji>sheep</kanji>.
羊.on: Stuck as a sheep, the king plays with a yo-yo all day to pass the time. A held 'yoh': <reading>よう</reading>.
羊.kun: The sheep king charges at the guards' car and 'hits a jeep!' Hits-jee, 'hee-tsu-jee': <reading>ひつじ</reading>, a sheep.

着.meaning: A <part>sheep</part> stands on top, and a long <part>slash</part> of yarn runs from its wool down past a big <part>eye</part> that never blinks. The eye watches you knit the yarn into a sweater, row by row. When it's done, you <kanji>don</kanji> it.
着.on: In your new sweater, you dance the cha-cha and trip on the last step. 'Cha' plus a hard k, 'chak': <reading>ちゃく</reading>.
着.kun: A brass key is knitted into the sweater's pocket. Key, then a soft 'roo': kee-roo, <reading>きる</reading>. <ja>着る</ja> is to wear.

遅.meaning: The <part>sheep</part>, still wearing its <part>horns</part> and <part>king</part> crown, walks down the <part>road</part> behind a <part>flag</part>, stopping to nibble every patch of grass. The parade behind it crawls. Everything is <kanji>slow</kanji>.
遅.on: A cheetah is stuck behind the sheep parade, panting with boredom. The first part of cheetah, 'chee': <reading>ち</reading>.
遅.kun: You check the cuckoo clock as the parade crawls by: 'Oh! Cuckoo!' Oh-koo: <reading>おくれる</reading>. <ja>遅れる</ja> is to be late.

交.meaning: At a party, <part>father</part> wears a paper <part>lid</part> for a hat, his legs crossing as he shuffles from guest to guest. He shakes every hand and joins every chat. He loves to <kanji>mingle</kanji>.
交.on: Father hands every guest an ice cream cone as he passes. Cone without the n, a held 'koh': <reading>こう</reading>.
交.kun: For each new guest, father pulls a coin from their ear: magic! The start of magic, 'mah-jee': <reading>まじわる</reading>. <ja>交わる</ja> is to mix.

安.meaning: A <part>woman</part> gets home, kicks off her shoes and flops onto the couch under her own <part>roof</part>. Phone off. Nobody needs her. At last she can <kanji>relax</kanji>.
安.on: She drops a ship's anchor beside the couch so nothing can move her. The first part of anchor, 'an': <reading>あん</reading>.
安.kun: 'Yah, sss…' she sighs, and the sigh fades away. Yah-soo: <reading>やすい</reading>. <ja>安い</ja> means cheap: lying on the couch costs nothing.

円.meaning: A coin purse <part>frame</part> stands open. Inside, a <part>pole</part> rests on a <part>one</part>-plank shelf, with coins stacked against it. Bump the purse and they roll out across the floor, each one a perfect <kanji>circle</kanji>.
円.on: The coins spin so fast they roar like an engine. The first part of engine, 'en': <reading>えん</reading>. It's also the yen, the coin itself.
円.kun: One coin rolls out to sea and ends up marooned on a tiny island. The start of marooned, 'mah-roo': <reading>まるい</reading>, round.

兄.meaning: A huge <part>mouth</part> on long <part>legs</part> struts around the house shouting orders at anyone smaller. Bossy, loud and a head taller than you: it's your <kanji>big brother</kanji>.
兄.on: Big brother eats the whole birthday cake before you get a slice. Cake, drop the k at the end, 'kay': <reading>けい</reading>.
兄.kun: His friend Annie laughs at him for eating it all. 'Annie', 'ah-nee': <reading>あに</reading>, big brother.

首.meaning: Two <part>horns</part> sit on a head that is nothing but a big <part>nose</part> with an <part>eye</part> peering out of it. It's so heavy that the poor creature needs a thick, strong <kanji>neck</kanji> to hold it up.
首.on: The creature bends its neck down to lick a pile of sugar cubes. The short first sound of sugar, 'shu': <reading>しゅ</reading>.
首.kun: At night it tucks its long neck into a cubby hole to sleep. Cubby, 'koo-bee': <reading>くび</reading>, the neck.

道.meaning: The horned creature stretches its <part>neck</part> along the <part>road</part>: <part>horns</part> first, <part>nose</part> sniffing every stone. Wherever its nose leads, it walks. Its trail becomes the <kanji>road-way</kanji>.
道.on: Along the road, the nose sniffs out a lump of bread dough. Dough is a held 'doh': <reading>どう</reading>.
道.kun: A meerkat and a cheetah race down the road after it. Mee from meerkat, chee from cheetah: <reading>みち</reading>, a road.

好.meaning: A <part>woman</part> scoops up a <part>child</part>, who squeals and grabs her hair and won't let go. Both of them are grinning. They're very <kanji>fond</kanji> of each other.
好.on: She buys the child an ice cream cone, and it ends up all over her hair. Cone without the n, a held 'koh': <reading>こう</reading>.
好.kun: The child loves her toy koala so much that when you ask to borrow it, she hugs it tight: 'Ko… no!' The short 'ko' of koala, then a firm 'no': <reading>このむ</reading>. <ja>好む</ja> is to like.

小.meaning: A short hook stands in the middle, and two crumbs fall off on either side. A toddler holds up a cookie that has just snapped: tiny bits everywhere. Everything about it is <kanji>little</kanji>.
小.on: For the little ones there's a tiny puppet show on a shoebox stage. Show is the held 'shoh': <reading>しょう</reading>.
小.kun: A cheetah cub, so little it can only squeak 'chee-ee!' Chee, then a long ee: <reading>ちいさい</reading>. <ja>小さい</ja> is small.

歩.meaning: A <part>stop</part> sign up top. Below it, a <part>little</part> kid with a <part>slash</part> of a stick. The kid stops at the sign, looks both ways, and goes on foot, one step, then another. That's how you <kanji>walk</kanji>.
歩.on: On the walk home, the kid stops for a hotdog. Its short first syllable, 'ho': <reading>ほ</reading>.
歩.kun: The dog walking beside the kid howls 'Ah-roooo!' at the hotdog. Ah-roo: <reading>あるく</reading>. <ja>歩く</ja> is to walk.

家.meaning: A <part>pig</part> moves in under your <part>roof</part>, takes the best bed and refuses to leave. It even hangs up a picture of itself. Now it isn't just your place: it's the pig's <kanji>house</kanji> too.
家.on: The pig eats every cabbage in the house, leaves and all. The short start of cabbage, 'ka': <reading>か</reading>.
家.kun: When you ask the pig to leave, it squeals 'Ee-eh!' and burrows under the blanket. Ee-eh: <reading>いえ</reading>, a house.

路.meaning: A <part>foot</part> stomps across the grass, dragging a <part>folding chair</part> behind it while a <part>mouth</part> mutters at every step. Foot after foot, chair legs scraping, they wear a line into the grass: a <kanji>path</kanji>.
路.on: A clanking robot follows the path too, beeping at each turn. The short first syllable of robot, 'ro': <reading>ろ</reading>.
路.kun: Then a muddy jeep bumps along the path and makes it even wider. Jeep, drop the p, 'jee': <reading>じ</reading>.

主.meaning: A <part>king</part> with a <part>dot</part> on top: one jewel on his crown, bigger than any other king's. When he enters the hall, every other king bows. He's the <kanji>lord</kanji> of them all.
主.on: At the feast, the lord takes all the sugar cubes for himself. The short first sound of sugar, 'shu': <reading>しゅ</reading>.
主.kun: At every meal the lord bangs his cup and says 'Oh, more!' Oh-moh, both short: <reading>おも</reading>.

味.meaning: A <part>mouth</part> waits beside a young fruit tree that isn't grown yet: one short new branch sits above the long one. The mouth can't wait and bites a hard green fruit. Sour, sharp, strange: a <kanji>flavor</kanji> it has never had.
味.on: A meerkat pops up beside the mouth to taste the fruit too. The first part of meerkat, 'mee': <reading>み</reading>.
味.kun: 'Ah, gee!' says the mouth, juice running down its chin, and reaches for another. Ah-jee: <reading>あじ</reading>, the taste.

力.meaning: One stroke bends like an arm with the elbow out, and a second stroke crosses it like a bulging <part>muscle</part>. Make a fist, flex, and feel the <kanji>power</kanji>.
力.on: A trio of strongmen flex together and the floor cracks. Drop the t of trio, 'ryo' said fast, then a hard k: 'ryok', <reading>りょく</reading>.
力.kun: A cheetah flexes and lifts a whole car over its head: 'Chee! Car! Ah!' Chee-kah-rah: <reading>ちから</reading>, strength.

田.meaning: A square split into four smaller squares, like farmland seen from a plane, with paths running between the plots. Each plot is flooded with water and planted with green shoots: a <kanji>rice field</kanji>.
田.on: A dentist sets up a chair in the middle of the field and pulls teeth among the shoots. The first part of dentist, 'den': <reading>でん</reading>.
田.kun: The farmer shows off the four neat plots with a bow: 'Ta-da!' Just the 'ta': <reading>た</reading>, a rice field.

男.meaning: A farmer heaves a whole <part>rice field</part> over his head, his <part>muscle</part> bulging underneath it. Mud drips down his arms. That field-lifter, in this kanji, is the <kanji>male</kanji>.
男.on: A dandelion growing in the lifted field blows its fluff right in his face. The first part of dandelion, 'dan': <reading>だん</reading>.
男.kun: He drops the field on a totem pole, and a koala tumbles off the top. 'Oh!' plus the short 'to' of totem and the 'ko' of koala: oh-to-ko, <reading>おとこ</reading>.

東.meaning: At dawn the <part>sun</part> peeks through a <part>tree</part>. The trunk is a <part>pole</part> running right through it, so the sun looks cut up like a <part>rice field</part>, with a <part>one</part>-line branch above. The sun always rises there: in the <kanji>east</kanji>.
東.on: The rising sun warms your toe first as it pokes out of the blanket. Toe, a held 'toh': <reading>とう</reading>.
東.kun: At sunrise in the east, a knight wobbles out on tall heels, garlic round his neck, holding up his shield against the glare. Hee from heel, ga from garlic, shee from shield: <reading>ひがし</reading>.

性.meaning: A gardener presses a stethoscope to a tiny <part>sprout</part> and listens to its <part>heartbeat</part>. 'Thump-thump… it's a girl!' she announces, like a vet with a new puppy. Every living thing has a <kanji>sex</kanji>, even a sprout.
性.on: The sprout grows tall and unfurls a sail at the top. Sail, drop the l, 'say': <reading>せい</reading>.
性.kun: A sprout's nature unfolds slowly, over years, like a long saga. 'Sah-gah', both short: <reading>さが</reading>, your nature.

乙.meaning: Two runners race. One runs straight; the other runs a crazy <part>zigzag</part> across the track and, of course, comes in second. Of those two, the zigzagger is always <kanji>the latter</kanji>.
乙.on: The zigzag runner stops halfway to munch a bag of oats. Say oats with a short o and let the s hiss into 'tsu': oh-tsu, <reading>おつ</reading>.
乙.kun: Zigzagging to the end, the runner crashes into a totem pole at the finish line. 'Oh!' then the short 'to' of totem: oh-to, <reading>おと</reading>.

雨.meaning: A flat sky line on top and a window frame hanging from it, with four drops running down the glass, two on each side of the bar. Look out of that window: it's <kanji>rain</kanji>.
雨.on: A soaked wolf sits outside the window and howls at the rain. Its short first part, 'woo': <reading>う</reading>.
雨.kun: The wolf shakes off the water and mutters 'Ah, meh,' wet and gloomy, not even bothering to howl again. Ah-meh: <reading>あめ</reading>, rain.

電.meaning: <part>rain</part> pours onto a <part>rice field</part>, and a <part>zigzag</part> of lightning hooks out of the bottom of the field, crackling. The field fizzes, and every bulb in the village lights up: <kanji>electricity</kanji>.
電.on: The village dentist plugs in her drill and it whirrs to life. The first part of dentist, 'den': <reading>でん</reading>.

停.meaning: A <part>leaning person</part> stops at a roadside hut: a <part>lid</part> roof, a <part>mouth</part> window, a <part>blanket</part> awning and a <part>one</part>-plank bench propped on a <part>crowbar</part>. The bus stops there too. Everything comes to a <kanji>halt</kanji>.
停.on: Someone runs sticky tape right across the road, so nobody can move on. Tape, drop the p, 'tay': <reading>てい</reading>.
停.kun: The bus halts nose to nose with a totem pole. The driver shrugs: 'Meh.' The short 'to' of totem, then 'meh': to-meh, <reading>とめる</reading>. <ja>停める</ja> is to stop.

付.meaning: A <part>leaning person</part> presses a sticker onto the wall with their <part>thumb</part>, hard, and holds it there for a whole minute. It isn't coming off now. It will <kanji>adhere</kanji> forever.
付.on: The sticker has been in a pocket all week and is covered in fuzz. A short, soft 'fu': <reading>ふ</reading>.
付.kun: Stick labels on two kettles: say 'two' with a hiss, then the 'ke' of kettle. Tsu-keh: <reading>つける</reading>. <ja>付ける</ja> is to attach.

立.meaning: A dot of a head, a wide hat line, two little strokes for legs, and a long line of ground under them. Someone who was slumped in a chair has just jumped up. They <kanji>stand up</kanji>.
立.on: A lizard stands up on its back legs to look around. The first part of lizard, 'liz', close to 'ritsu': <reading>りつ</reading>.
立.kun: You stand up and bow: 'Ta-da!' Swap the 'da' for a hissed 'tsu': ta-tsu, <reading>たつ</reading>. <ja>立つ</ja> is to stand.

番.meaning: Farmers line up at the <part>rice field</part>, each holding a <part>sieve</part> full of <part>rice</part>. One by one they shake it out over the plots. 'Next!' Everyone waits for their <kanji>turn</kanji>.
番.on: Whoever's turn it is gets to play the banjo while they sow. The first part of banjo, 'ban': <reading>ばん</reading>.
番.kun: Two swans, always a pair, paddle up for their turn. One sneezes 'tsu!' and the other gets a bulb of garlic stuck in its beak: 'ga!' Tsu-ga: <reading>つがい</reading>, a pair.
